req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The violation is test[5] (test_head_delete_also_returns_405) which has kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is only valid for positive tests that exercise valid state transitions. For a negative test verifying that an unsupported HTTP method is rejected, the correct heuristic is NEG (negative equivalence class / error pathway). Fix: change heuristic from STC to NEG on test[5]. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were.

tests.name: test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing pre-loaded rows
No authentication required to trigger the 405 — method check happens before auth
actions: Send GET request to /2/delete without any session cookie
expected: Response status_code is exactly 405 (not 404, not 403, not 200)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_get_delete_returns_405_for_valid_post()

tests.name: test_post_delete_does_not_return_405_when_authenticated
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing pre-loaded rows
Post id=2 exists and is authored by user Rahul (id=1)
User Rahul is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: Send POST request to /2/delete with the authenticated session
trace: R-FLASKR-030: POST method must be accepted (not rejected with 405)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_post_delete_does_not_return_405_when_authenticated():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_post_delete_does_not_return_405_when_authenticated()

tests.name: test_get_delete_allow_header_contains_post_only
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing pre-loaded rows
expected: Allow header is present and contains POST
Allow header does NOT contain GET
trace: R-FLASKR-030: route registered with methods=('POST',) only; Allow header must reflect this
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_delete_allow_header_contains_post_only():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    allow = r.headers.get('Allow', '')
    assert 'POST' in allow
    assert 'GET' not in allow

tests.name: test_head_delete_also_returns_405
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing pre-loaded rows
actions: Send HEAD request to /2/delete (HEAD is also not in the allowed methods)
expected: HTTP 405 — HEAD is not POST, so it must also be rejected
trace: R-FLASKR-030: any non-POST method must be rejected; HEAD is a state-transition variant of GET
tests.executable:

def test_head_delete_also_returns_405():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.open('/2/delete', method='HEAD')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 302
